One of the best things about miniseries is that, because of their short runtime, they have to make every minute count. A miniseries that isn’t engaging in the first few moments is unlikely to achieve much success. But the ones that can catch the audience’s attention right from the opening often climb to the greatest heights. In recent years, Netflix has become the home of some of the greatest miniseries of this century, proudly housing several such shows that do a fantastic job of engaging the audience within the very first minutes.

In fact, many of these miniseries start strong and keep building, compelling the viewer to watch the entire thing with rapt attention. Though they range from critically acclaimed genre gems to cult hits and niche favorites, these highly engaging miniseries are all masterpieces of the single-season, self-contained story format. Now, without further ado, here’s our handpicked selection of near-perfect Netflix miniseries that successfully hooked us within the first five minutes.

blocks.c: Jharrel Jerome as Korey Wise in 'When They See Us'

blocks.x: Ava DuVernay’s multi-award-winning true crime drama When They See Us is a tragic retelling of a real-life case from 1989, in which five teenage boys of color were wrongfully accused of assaulting a Caucasian American woman in Central Park, New York City. The four-part series recounts the fateful event, followed by their arrests, and how the case completely upended the lives of these five young men and their families in the years to come. Asante Blackk, Caleel Harris, Jharrel Jerome, Ethan Herisse, and Marquis Rodriguez portray the five central characters.

One of the most critically acclaimed crime-drama miniseries of the last decade, When They See Us takes an incisive look at our dysfunctional social systems and raises important questions. The story opens with the five boys enjoying an ordinary day in the spring of 1989 in their Harlem neighborhood, but soon shifts to chaos and darkness when the group finds themselves in the wrong place at the wrong time. While deeply unsettling, the first minutes of When They See Us are quite compelling and encourage the viewer to watch more, drawing you into a harrowing but eye-opening true story.

blocks.c: Andrew Scott as Tom Ripley looking out the window in Episode 4 of Netflix's Ripley

blocks.x: Steven Zaillian’s miniseries adaptation of Patricia Highsmith’s crime bestseller, The Talented Mr. Ripley, Netflix’s Ripley is a neo-noir psychological thriller about the titular conman, Tom, who is hired by a wealthy New Yorker to bring his wayward son, Dickie, back home from Italy. Tom goes to Italy but finds himself tempted by Dickie's romantic life and develops a dangerous obsession, sending him down a dark and deadly path. The show boasts a phenomenal cast led by Andrew Scott as Tom Ripley, with Johnny Flynn, Dakota Fanning, Eliot Sumner, and more in key roles.

A very Hitchcockian thriller, Ripley is a deliberate blend of jarring narrative styles, striking visual atmosphere, and a quiet paranoia creeping in with every passing minute that grips attention right from the start. The series opens with a highly stylized but disorienting black-and-white sequence that reminds us of Giallo films and classic expressionism, acting as a flash-forward before the actual story begins. From the staging, scene setting, and the striking cinematography in the very first minutes to the enigmatic ending, Ripley is by far the best interpretation of Tom Ripley we’ve seen on screen so far.

blocks.c: Donny staring at his computer in the dark looking concerned in Baby Reindeer.

blocks.x: Scottish actor and comedian Richard Gadd created and stars in this semi-autobiographical dark comedy thriller miniseries, based on his one-man show of the same name. In Baby Reindeer, Gadd plays Donny, an aspiring comedian and bartender whose life is turned upside down when a friendly gesture towards a customer named Martha leads her to an obsession, and he’s forced to confront the shadows of his own past. Jessica Gunning co-stars as Martha, with Nava Mau and Tom Goodman-Hill as other key characters.

Beginning in media res, Baby Reindeer does not ease us into the story; it thrusts us directly into Donny’s misery even before we get to know him, immediately encouraging us to find out more about his life and what led him to the first scene. Sharply written and well-performed, Baby Reindeer takes an intense look at the human condition and buried trauma. Widely praised for its direction and acting, particularly for Gunning’s breakout performance, Baby Reindeer ranks among Netflix’s top miniseries produced in the 2020s.

blocks.c: A young boy in the anime Pluto

blocks.x: Pluto is an anime series adaptation of the Astro Boy spin-off manga, Pluto: Urasawa X Tezuka by Naoki Urasawa and Takashi Nagasaki. Robots and humans cohabit in a future world where a series of brutal murders of important human and robot personalities shakes their uneasy balance. A robot detective named Gesicht from Europol begins investigating and discovers a decades-old conspiracy in motion that could destroy the world humans and machines have built together. Directed by Toshio Kawaguchi, Pluto stars the voices of Shinshū Fuji, Hiroki Yasumoto, Koichi Yamadera, Yoko Hikasa, and Minori Suzuki.

Pluto is an extraordinary anime miniseries that combines the sci-fi, philosophical drama, murder mystery, and political thriller genres into a highly intriguing narrative style. In the first five minutes, the series successfully sets the foundations of an apocalyptic tragedy and welcomes the audience to a chilling whodunit investigation that slowly unfolds into a more serious meditation on humanity. Exceptionally written, animated, and performed, Pluto is a remarkable miniseries that attracts attention with its brilliant style and art while engaging the mind with some truly profound themes.

blocks.c: Carla Gugino as the Red Death in Netflix’s 'The Fall of the House of Usher'

blocks.x: A modern gothic thriller at its best, Fall of the House of Usher is Mike Flanagan’s deliciously diabolical interpretation of Edgar Allan Poe’s short story of the same name. Also inspired by other works of Poe, the eight-episode series follows the titular family’s story of corruption, tragedy, and redemption, where the brother-sister duo Roderick and Madeline are forced to pay the price of their sins by a mysterious woman named Verna. Carla Gugino, Bruce Greenwood, Mary McDonnell, Mark Hamill, and more star as the main characters.

The Fall of the House of Usher delights and terrifies in the same breath, with a stylish and rich visual style and an equally intense psychological horror narrative. The first few minutes of the show set a chilling atmosphere, preparing the viewer for what is about to come, when Roderick confesses to his felonies and finally explains the bizarre, impossible deaths of his children. From here on, every turn of The Fall of the House of Usher is a slow, wicked slide into madness, full of unexpected shocks and surprises.

Created by Paul Tomalin, Bodies is an underrated sci-fi mystery thriller miniseries adapted from the DC Vertigo graphic novel of the same name by Si Spencer, centering on the discovery of a mysterious dead body in an obscure London alley in four different timelines. Four determined detectives, in their respective timelines, set out to solve the puzzle, uncovering a time-bending and life-threatening conspiracy. Stephen Graham, Jacob Fortune-Lloyd, Shira Haas, Amaka Okafor, and Kyle Soller star as the primary protagonists.

Bodies is a fun fusion of sci-fi, murder mystery, and historical drama, where each genre seamlessly fits in with the other. The series is addictive right from the start, capturing the audience’s complete attention with a high-stakes chase and then exposing them directly to the mysterious corpse before shifting the scene from the present to the past. The deliberate chaos of this back-and-forth narrative is what compels the viewer to indulge in the cerebral thrill of Bodies.

blocks.c: Owen Cooper sat wearing a green t-shirt in 'Adolescence'

blocks.x: The most critically acclaimed psychological crime drama of 2025, Jack Thorne and Stephen Graham’s Adolescence is an emotionally heavy exploration of teenage crime and every parent’s worst fear. When 13-year-old Jamie Miller is charged with the murder of his fellow school student, his life is torn apart between heartbroken parents, law and order, and a skewed social system. Owen Cooper plays Jamie, with Graham as his father, Eddie. The series also stars Erin Doherty, Christine Tremarco, Ashley Walters, Faye Marsay, and more as key characters.

At the time of its premiere, Adolescence became a massive success and a highly impactful teen crime drama with major social and political impact, particularly within the UK. While the show is definitely mentally jarring from the beginning, it is the long-take filming that hooks the audience right away, moving without a blink between one tension-packed scene and the next. Adolescence has since left a lasting impression on the crime drama genre and set new standards for miniseries, proving that sometimes shorter series can speak louder than their longer counterparts.
